fact: The Central Bank of Eswatini says a consumer unsatisfied with a financial institution's response to a complaint can escalate it to the CBE's Ombudsman, and that the Market Conduct and Consumer Protection Unit supervises institutions including mobile money service providers.
system: CBE Ombudsman / Market Conduct and Consumer Protection Unit

fact: The World Bank FSAP note says the Central Bank of Eswatini's 2019 Mobile Money Transfer Practice Note sets limited consumer-protection and conduct requirements for mobile money providers, which banks and mobile money providers have generally been complying with.
system: Mobile Money Transfer (MMT) Practice Note No.1/2019/NPSS

fact: The World Bank FSAP note says a CBE Ombudsman and an FSRA Ombudsman have been in place for several years taking complaints about credit, transaction and savings products, the CBE one without finalized procedural rules.
The World Bank FSAP note reports complaint figures from the ombudsman schemes' last annual reports: 40 complaints to the CBE Ombudsman and 84 to the FSRA Ombudsman, up from 59 the year before.

The Central Bank of Eswatini's Practice Note No.1/2019/NPSS for mobile money service providers, in force from 5 March 2019, sets consumer-protection rules on fee disclosure, written customer contracts and complaints handling.
system: Practice Note for Mobile Money Service Providers

fact: The Practice Note requires mobile money providers to run a complaints desk and free hotline, and lets an unsatisfied complainant escalate an unresolved decision to the Central Bank of Eswatini.
system: Practice Note for Mobile Money Service Providers

fact: The proposed National Payment System Regulations, 2026, before Eswatini's Senate, include consumer protection provisions alongside electronic funds transfers and payment service provider obligations.
